estimate_emissions.description: Estimate the CO2 that comes with using some electricity over a period of up to 31 days, such as a car's charging session or a month of meter readings, for Great Britain, a country, a region or a postcode. The energy is taken as used evenly over the period, and each half hour counts at NESO's estimated actual carbon intensity where there is one, otherwise its forecast. Time the service has no figures for counts at the average of the rest, and the result says how much that was. No API key required.

find_lowest_carbon_time.description: Find when to run something that uses electricity for a set time, such as charging a car, a wash or a batch job, so that it uses the lowest-carbon electricity: the start, within the next 24 hours or a window of up to 48 as far as NESO's forecast reaches, with the lowest average carbon intensity for Great Britain, a country, a region or a postcode. uk_time.description: The same span on the UK clock, e.g. '14:00 to 14:30 BST on Fri 25 Sep'.

postcode.description: The first half of the postcode the figures were asked for with, e.g. 'RG10'. Null when a region was chosen.

region_id.description: The service's number for the area: 1 to 14 for the regions, 15 to 17 for England, Scotland and Wales, 18 for Great Britain.

get_intensity_statistics.description: Get Great Britain's highest, average and lowest carbon intensity over a period of up to 30 days, with the service's index for the average, and optionally the same for each block of 1 to 24 hours in it, such as each day. Past half hours count at NESO's estimated actual and future ones at their forecast. No API key required.

get_intensity_statistics.name: get_intensity_statistics

parameters.description: The start of the period. A date alone, such as 2026-09-24, is midnight at the start of that day in the UK, and any date or time written without a time zone is read as UK time.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: The end of the period, up to 30 days after the start as the hours pass (720 hours), which across the October clock change is an hour short of 30 days on the UK clock. Leave empty for a day after the start on the UK clock, so a date alone gives that whole day.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: Also split the period into blocks of this many hours, from 1 to 24, each with its own highest, average and lowest: 24 gives one block a day. When the period does not divide into whole blocks, the last one is shorter. Leave empty for the whole period only.
parameters.name: block_hours

block_hours.description: The block length asked for, or null.

blocks.description: Each block, in order, when a block length was given; otherwise empty. The last ends with the period, so it is shorter when the period does not divide into whole blocks.

from.description: When it starts, in UTC (ISO 8601), e.g. 2026-09-25T13:00:00Z.

index.description: The service's index for the average: 'very low' to 'very high'.

max.description: The highest half hour, in gCO2/kWh.

min.description: The lowest half hour, in gCO2/kWh.

description: Get the carbon intensity of electricity in Great Britain from the Carbon Intensity API of National Energy System Operator (NESO): the figure now, a half-hourly forecast up to two days ahead and past figures, for Great Britain, England, Scotland, Wales, 14 regions or a postcode. Find the lowest-carbon time to run something, estimate the CO2 of electricity used, compare regions and see the mix of fuels. No account or API key required.
